newsitem.title: SLOVAKIA: Slovak VZS signs debt restructuring deal with ING.
newsitem.headline: Slovak VZS signs debt restructuring deal with ING.

text.p: Slovakia's largest steel producer VSZ a.s. said on Monday it had signed an agreement with ING Barings to restructure its $125 million international syndicated loan extended in March last year.
VSZ Finance Director Jozef Burian told Reuters the loan will be refinanced to London Interbank Offered Rate (LIBOR) plus 0.70 percent, from a margin of 1.4 percent over LIBOR.
He said the credit repayment period would be extended to five years, from the original maturity of three years.
"We signed the agreement with the lead manager last Friday, and the new conditions will be valid from next March."

The credit extended in March 1996 by a syndicate of 18 banks led by ING Barings London, was to have been used to restructure the company's old loans and to help finance operational and investment needs.

Last month, VSZ signed a five-year, $50 million revolving credit, lead managed by Chase Manhattan. The company said it might draw further loans this year, but that it would focus mainly on credits with five-year and longer maturities.
VSZ said it expected to post an unconsolidated, 1996 after-tax profit of around 1.3 billion crowns, up some 100 million crowns from 1995.
